review:
I tried to avoid jumping on the hype train/bandwagon after being burned by BF2042 (still pissed about that). I spent a week just watching people stream the game and give their two cents. After a few beers and continuously disconnecting or being unable to load into EFT'S PvE servers, I decided I'd grab the $35 version of this game to make sure I could run it on my hardware. If I couldn't, I'd just get a refund.. no big deal. I played for an entire day, and forgot to eat. I witnessed the devs issue hotfixes on the fly as I played. Their level of proactivity, drive, and passion I find to be very refreshing. They even read our Reddit posts on the weekends, so that they can make necessary adjustments based on player feedback.
The second day I played, I upgraded to the Gray Zone Supporter edition because of how much fun I had playing with some friends all day. I haven't spent much time in the PvP servers so I can't really speak to that. This game sort of reminds of the vibes I would get playing R6: Vegas 2 terrorist hunt with your friends. But now there's elements of open world exploration, cooperative play with other players, and quest/trader progression. 
While I do think there are a lot of aspects that need tweaking and extra attention, my experience has been one that I have not had for quite some time. And after I log out, I don't have to worry about insurance timers. You can pick this up and put it down at your leisure. Some of us have responsibilities.
They said this wasn't the Tarkov killer, but it helped me Escape from Tarkov.

P.S. I just want to make this abundantly clear. I did not purchase Tarkov's Unheard edition, nor will I ever. I have been playing on and off with an EOD account since 2017 or so, and was granted access to the PvE. They're dishing it out in waves to EOD owners.

So far I've played this game 35 hours, all in the PVE mode called Joint Operations. This review is more for semi relaxed tactical shooter fans who don't care about sweaty PVP or K/D ratios. I usually don't post reviews, but with the brigading that took place with this title I felt the need to review it positively.

TLDR review: At launch this game is pretty fun, especially in the PVE mode (for me). I bought the $35 base version and plan to upgrade to the $100 supporter edition.

Pros:
- Top tier weapon dynamic, customization, physics and firefighting. Better then COD or Battlefield, very similar to Tarkov, and arguably similar to games like Squad, Arma, etc. There are some weapon and projectile dynamics bugs at launch, but overall I think its a good balance between an arcade shooter like COD and a full on sim like Arma or Squad. Even just seeing the gas blowback when you shoot with a suppressor cluod your scope is something I have never seen in a game before and is a real life touch.
- Amazing visuals, possibly best looking shooter on the market at time of review. Not as polished as a AAA game as far as performance, but the visuals are top notch if you have the hardware to run it.
- Huge open world map that you can literally walk for hours and hours through, with a really high attention to detail. Some assets were definately reused, but each major location feels distinct
- An amazing coop experience. The fact they launched with VOIP and it seems like 90% of players both use it and communicate in the battlefield with it is amazing. So many other games you barely hear other players in the game, but in this one you almost always hears players working together, offering help with a mission, even sometimes from the other factions. I haven't seen or heard a toxic player yet.
- One of the best medical systems in a game, bar none. The only better medical systems I've seen is something like KAT medical in arma (a mod) and some medical mods in squad.

Neither cons or pros:
- I do think the game play loop may be a bit repetitive. I still don't see what end game content looks like, but the main game play loop is - get a quest to explore a new area, then 3 quests to find or pickup or deliver something to the area, then kill the boss. Its definitely been fun, but I worry it might get old.
- I also worry about the long term support. Unlike squad where servers are hosted by third parties, if the devs run out of money this game will be dead in the water. I usually don't like to support these types of games. This developer has only created mobile games so keep that in mind.
- It seems like for performance at launch there is a mixed bag. Here is another point of data for those who are curious: I have AMD 5800X3D, 32gb of ram, and a 4080 super. At 4k I get around 100fps with max settings DLSS on, 60fp with it off. My GPU usage is 90% and CPU usage is around 20%.

Cons (overall):
Currently none. There are many cons to this game, but I see them being fixed long term. I will update this in a few months though.

Cons (launch only - hoping these are fixed):
- As many have mentioned, the server situation, especially for US servers and during peak gaming hours, are pretty bad. There is a lot of stuttering, walking in place, etc. Even on a good server, throwing a grenade results in watching the grenade move, pause, move, pause, etc. Leaving your server and rejoining fixes this most of the time, but sometimes it takes 4 or 5 times trying to rejoin to even get in a new server.
- The projectile physics are bizarre. It seems like 5.56 and 5.45 does more damage then 7.62, as well as shooting through windows, huts, fences, bushes can be a mixed bag with different outcomes. Sometimes an AI takes one head shot, sometimes 3.
- There is a no time of day/weather at launch, but the devs have said they will add this.
- The only using little birds for transportation is currently just not enough. I'm not even talking about people camping LZs on PVP, as much as its just an annoying and painful to use mechanic. The devs have said they will add basecamps, which will be good but I still think an ATV or something similar would be nice.

Things I would like the devs to add (at launch - will update if they add them):
- Searching and filtering in the vendor menus
- See linked items in the item description - i.e. a flash hider necessary for a suppressor or a plate adapter for a sight.
- Turn in quests from quests tab of tablet
- Other people should be able to loot your body in PVE mode if you die twice or disconnect
- Keys, especially quest required ones need to be less RNG. I still have not found most quest required keys despite clearing the mobs in area several times.
- Audio needs to be reworked. Footsteps and bush moving is essentially inaudible, while gunshots are too loud with headsets on. The different ear pro either just mute everything (razer) or make everything louder (gssh).

I do enjoy the game, it has some things that needs to be fixed but I still do recommend the game and it will just become better with time. (This is what I think)

So if you are okay with playing an EA (Early Access) game, as you know they might have some bugs/issues and not be top-notch state, then go a head and get it now.

If not, I would say to wait until they fix a few more things.

This game has a ton of potential. MADFINGER, if you're reading this, please look further below for some more direct feedback.

For experienced players of games like Escape From Tarkov, Arena Breakout Infinite, etc, many aspects of the game will be intuitive. Inventory management, weapon customization, equipment slots (with some additions/changes, like being able to wear a tactical belt) will be quite familiar.

The real draw for this game, in my opinion, is the more free-form style of gameplay in place of "raids". You don't have any raid timer, ever. You aren't restricted by timers or boundaries pretty much at all. You can go where you want, when you want. That is extremely cool to have in a game like this.
I think people underestimate the importance of immersion in the extraction shooter genre (which this game effectively falls within, just in a pretty unique kind of way). Games like Tarkov are successful in part because they build such a convincing world. This game does much the same, just with a very different tone. The fact that you can just "live" in this world without restrictions really creates a special feeling that's hard to describe.

Somewhat on the topic of making comparisons with Tarkov, something I really enjoyed about this game (mostly) is the amount of direction they give you with the tasks. I have completed all but 1 or 2 tasks so far (up to the introduction of Ban Pa, in other words: leaving the starter town) without needing any wikis or anything of the sort. I just read what they told me to do and figured it out on my own. WAY easier to follow directions (for most of the tasks) than Tarkov. I'm unsure if this is due to a language barrier issue or just a different approach in design, but either way it was a refreshing boost in immersion to not have to constantly rely on wikis for basic info.


Criticisms/feedback for MADFINGER:

1. -- The game is extremely unclear with VERY important rules involving death and item retrieval. There are very important specific rules in place that the player must know in order to competently approach retrieving their items after death (because yes, after you die, you're still in the same server and you can go back to attempt retrieving your items). i.e. you have 1 hour before your body despawns, and you can ONLY retrieve your MOST RECENT body's items. If you die 2+ times then you can only loot your most recent body. All others will be marked as "old loot", for some reason. This limitation can be completely circumvented by simply being in a squad with other players and having them take the items off your body and throw them on the ground, making the whole feature kinda pointless except for the fact that it puts solo players at a further disadvantage in a pretty arbitrary and immersion-breaking way. The wording is confusing as well. Since it says "old" I thought that it was based on a timer. I needed another player to explain it to me before I realized that dying a second time caused it.

My personal take here? Just remove the "old loot" thing that gets applied after multiple deaths entirely. This only serves to make the experience more frustrating for solos, especially new ones getting bullied by more experienced players/squads.

2. -- The ammunition and armor systems are very confusing. I get almost zero sense of progression when I find anything new, because there's no clear system for what's better/worse. Even a simple instructional chart or something to decipher what I'm looking at would be nice. A huge part of the progression and motivation for players in a looting-based game is to give a clear "Ah HA!" moment when the player finds something good or unlocks the ability to purchase good gear/ammo of their own. Currently, I only get this feeling with guns, and absolutely nothing else. So far, I have almost zero understanding of how any of the armor or ammunition types work. The most clear thing I've seen so far was a description for ammo describing it as sub-sonic, but with the greatly reduced muzzle velocity, I can only assume that it's less effective in SOME other way, I just don't know what's affected. Penetration? Damage? Bullet drop when shooting at a distance? Absolutely no idea what's affected or how it relates with anyone's armor, and more importantly, I don't have any idea HOW MUCH any of those things might be affected. Someone gave me a plate carrier and told me "that's the best one in the game" and the only difference I could find that particularly stood out was the addition of a little "+" next to the armor class, and I have no idea what that means.

3. -- I really like the design choice of having the "marked as aggressor" status placed on players with varying duration depending on the severity of their friendly fire. However, I think that the game is currently overly harsh in cases of immediate defense.
Example: I was walking into hostile territory with 1 teammate by my side. From behind, someone opened fire at us at about 30 meters out, hitting and wounding my teammate and continuing to open fire into his body, and within ~2 seconds, I swiveled around and gunned down the aggressor, who turned out to be a confused ally who mistook us for the enemies that were a little further ahead. When I shot him, I quickly landed a fatal blow, killing him in defense of my teammate with absolutely zero chance to react. I was given 57 minutes of aggressor status for that, even though I literally saved someone's life while the dude was mid-fire, full auto. While I understand that it is not good to encourage "revenge friendly fire", I think there's a line that needs to be drawn when you're quite literally saving the life of an innocent teammate in defense of a rogue ally, regardless if that ally is intentionally acting out or not. Everyone involved was cool with each other there, no heated emotions or anything, and everyone involved agreed that it was unfair for me to get ~1hr with the aggressor status.


Anyway, thanks for reading. There's way more good and bad I could say about the game, but overall I've found it to be a unique and enjoyable experience, so I recommend the game. I just hope that concerns like these are taken seriously and addressed. I'll likely update my review with coming updates to the game.

To preface this review, I play exclusively PVE and most of the time solo. With that being said I have greatly enjoyed the gameplay loop it scratches the tactical shooter itch for me without having to worry about any of the BS that comes with PVP experiences like Tarkov. Or having to always have a 4 person party like in some of the other extraction or objective based shooters. Now don't get me wrong all those games have their place but this game allows me as a working father of 2 the opportunity to sit down for an hour or two before bed and just enjoy the game at my own pace. I've enjoyed what has come out this far and am looking forward to what is coming next. If you are looking for a more casual tactical shooter experience, that still has most of the systems that the more hardcore contemporaries of this game have, it's worth picking up.

Let me start off by saying I want this game to succeed more than anyone, and why I opted for the supporter edition, It's the open world tactical fps game I've always wanted. A hybrid of Ghost Recon and Tarkov, that reaches that itch that the latter can't. However there are some extreme disappointments that has me worried for the success and future of the game.


The AI is one of the main things besides poor optimization that just ruins the fun for me, I could write a novel about all the issues with the AI but I'll just list a few of the main ones. 

[olist]
    [*]I can't count the number of times I've died and amount of gear I've lost to AI pulling off 200 yard, hip-firing 1 taps. It's just ridiculous and it needs to be addressed ASAP.

    [*]Another thing is the AI's detection capabilities, being the main game ruiner for me; there's absolutely no reason while I'm shooting at AI suppressed, within foliage, from 200 yards away the AI should be able to turn 180 degrees, know my exact position and return fire pin-point accurate fire (again off the hip).

    [*]Goes with the previous point, but the AI's ability to see through foliage is insane. If I can't see them, they shouldn't be able to see me.
[/olist]


As far as optimization, the main issue I've encountered as well as others are spiking CPU temps. There doesn't seem to be any specific event that causes it, as my PC has hit thermal protection and crashed several times (Ryzen 5900x with an AIO) causing complete gear losses. It does seem to happen more frequently around helicopters, but has happened everywhere.


The vendor levels/rep and items they sell needs to be re-evaluated. Two things don't make sense to me.
[olist]
    [*]Why am I being tasked to go to locations where the AI is wearing III+ Armor and firing M855, when I only have reliable access to FMJ and at best IIIA armor? That's just a recipe for not a fun time. Also the fact that a bunch of good ammo is just not sold by vendors anymore. What happened to M855A1/M856A1 and BP/PP?
    [*]Since this update is based around night vision, I find the decision odd why the best night vision not offered by any vendor (same for AK308). This is an early access, so I'd figure being able to reliably test and experience content in the game is paramount. For a full release I see item rarity/scarcity, but in a test version?
[/olist]


The final thing I'd like to mention is the time frame of major updates, I was very disheartened when the road-map released to see content bearing updates were only scheduled on a semi-annual basis, is that a joke? Before night-ops I had stopped playing for a good 4-5 months as the content had just dried up. No new features, no new weapons or gear to play with, no new quests. Is this what I can expect from the game? Playing for a bit, getting bored, and having to wait 6 months for a new update? Why can't we have minor content bearing updates more often? Having past game development experience, and vast amounts of modding experience; I know it is not a big task or ask for a large studio to pump out some new weapons, gear, or quests within the minor patches to keep the player base alive and interested. I also seriously hope you're joking about not implementing vehicles into the game, that would be just a downright suicidal development choice and I hope to not expect that from this studio... I won't go into the hundreds of quality of life suggestions I have.

For now until some of these rather game breaking issues get addressed, and the devs can step up and show they're committed to maintaining their player base by delivering new content in a reasonable manner, and not just farming funding and posting employee interviews that (just being honest here) no one cares about while the game turns into vaporware; I'd say save your money, and keep an eye on the reviews.

I enjoyed Gray Zone Warfare early on, but over time several decisions have pushed me away from the game.

One of the biggest issues has been the increasing focus on Twitch campaigns and exclusive rewards. A large portion of the community has voiced opposition to locking items behind Twitch promotions, yet criticism often seems to be met with locked threads, removed discussions, or heavy moderation rather than meaningful engagement. The backlash to the most recent campaign became one of the most upvoted negative discussions on Reddit in less than 24 hours, which should be a sign that many players are unhappy with the direction.

The gameplay itself also suffers from growing frustration. Cheating has become increasingly common, to the point where it feels comparable to other extraction shooters that struggle with the same problem, perhaps even approaching Tarkov levels at times.

PvE has its own issues. Many PVP focused players use PvE servers to farm loot rather than their PVPVE server, clearing valuable areas and killing HVTs for gear before others can reach them. Players trying to complete missions often spend hours searching for a target that has already been killed with low respawns or arriving at locations that have been completely stripped. Those same players can then transfer back to PvPvE servers with the gear they acquired and focus purely on PvP.

This creates massive time sinks and takes much of the enjoyment out of PvE. A few months ago, I spent three days trying to complete one mission that required killing an HVT and another that required finding a specific key. Every attempt was ruined by players repeatedly farming those locations before anyone else could complete their objectives. In the end, the friends I had bought copies of the game for became so frustrated that they quit and never looked back. Time is limited, and wasting multiple days because mission progress depends on competing with loot farmers is simply not fun.

Without private servers (not their idea of private servers with is servers for select twitch streamers with special controls for them) or a true friends-only option, players who simply want to enjoy cooperative PvE are forced to compete with server looters and campers.

EDIT: Decided to hop back in after not playing for a few months. First PvE mission I clear, the entire area solo. I move towards a building doorway to get the objective, and suddenly a player who had been hiding in the tree line the entire time, never helping kill anything, just watching and comes sprinting in full tilt straight to the loot box, grabs everything, and immediately runs back out.
Likely just a loot runner, one of the toxic PvP-only crowd using PvE as a gear farm. Yep, guess every move doesn't matter. Well, I'm dropping it again for another few months.

So, having played Tarkov for a few years and the numerous comparisons surfacing at launch and even now I'll give a quick disclaimer. This game is properly using alpha, meaning it is by no means release ready, that being said it has updates queued by the devs till 2028 and further planned.

The game has a good foundation, their asking price is correct, and overall the game seems to have a bright future. The Devs are somewhat new to creating PC games, as they have mostly created mobile games, but they are doing a damn good job. This game is not Tarkov, though it has many aspects of it, the systems are streamlined, the storage while being the classic STALKER/A RPG stack loot is not as painfully difficult to deal with. Overall, if you enjoy the idea of Tarkov but don't want to PVP all the time, this game is solid. Though be warned, PVE is the focal point, pvp is something you have to seek out.

Get the game if you are ready for an Alpha with all the bugs and issues behind it, don't get it if you're expecting something polished with just a few updates.

The good.:
-Gun customization that will match most other games, though the weapons are limited.
-No loading screens outside of getting into the match, meaning you can walk across the entire world.
-Immersive ambient noises, from flies going towards your ears to the normal insect sounds in the background.
-Constant Dev feedback and updates, within the first few months till now there has been a consistent dialogue between the devs and players.
-Simplified ammo, looking towards Tarkov there is not a pool of over 100 different rounds that you will never use polluting the loot pool.
-Graphics while not polished are lovely especially the beard physics, again alpha game so optimization is not there, but the devs did release what settings to press to fix a issues like low frames, stutters and the like.

The Mediocre/Soon to be changed.
-Pistols and shotguns were all but useless, this change is coming next patch this fall so could be a day after this review or a few weeks.
-Helicopters choking up people coming and going, this is being adjusted in said patch.
-Lootable Valuables are coming in, how this is implemented may change to be good are bad.
-A.I. is basic if not over tuned, think Tarkov Raiders/Rogues/scavs, soon this will be changed. At the moment some act like scavs, then they will suddenly become rogues or raiders. Also, if you play tarkov PVE currently the AI reacts with the same hivemind.
-Limited weapon choices, though more are coming in along with the day night cycle with NVGs and actual night missions and more points of interest.
-Quest keys are hard to come by, they will now have world spawns.
-The UI for shopping and tasks is simplified, though some hotkeys are a bit testy.

The bad
-The game is in Alpha so mechanics and bugs are available, along with growing pains.
-PVP is not a focus of the Devs, the map is larger than the average battlefield map so don't expect any good pvp unless you plan on walking to a place setting up to fight in compounds.
-No squad progression yet, I believe they are adding it in with the next update, but I could be wrong.

This game scratches the Tarkov itch really well while being a little more forgiving to play. This game does not require a crazy amount of time in game to learn, it's fairly easy to pick up and start playing and be moderately good in. I love the aspect that you can choose to play more mission oriented with vendor tasks than how Tarkov does it. 

Some negative reviews are founded, this is what I agree with: the AI can be stupid quick to headshot you from very far away, the game is demanding and frame rate can drop at times, and a lot of the world seems to be fairly empty vegetation.

Mostly, all of these negative points are overcome through gameplay. For example, you quickly learn how to engage the AI to not get killed really easily. Adjusting graphics settings depending on your set up. The cities and towns are so well designed and full of exploration and exciting gunfights.

I own the Supporter Edition, play PvE, and this is a review from 0.4 (Spearhead) onwards.  I played this game when it first released into Early Access, and I saw the vision of what it could be.  I quit shortly after because the environments, though beautiful, were empty.  The AI loved shooting through bushes, and the performance was terrible.  The tasks were designed to move you around the map, but the world lacked a hook to draw you in.

These issues have all been addressed.  Although I admittedly have an insanely powerful PC, I haven't dipped below 200 FPS on 1440p Ultra.  The world feels lived in, and I often get distracted from quests because I want to explore a building or take on a pod of enemies.  The world is incredibly immersive, and I applaud their decision to lean more into Ghost Recon and away from Tarkov.  I haven't been killed through a bush yet, and stealth feels not only viable, but satisfying.   There is now lootable and readable lore to be discovered throughout the map, and post it notes on guard outposts have passwords to locked loot rooms.  Exploration is a delight, and is vaguely reminiscent of immersive sims.  I'm so excited to take on bunkers, bosses, and discover all that this game has to offer now that the rough edges have been polished down enough to make the game itself fun to play.

I genuinely love what Gray Zone Warfare is building here. The gunplay feels excellent, the weapon systems are deep, and the overall tactical pacing is exactly what I want from a realism-focused shooter. When everything clicks, it’s intense in the best way.

Visually? It’s a masterpiece. The atmosphere and environmental detail make it one of the best-looking tactical shooters out right now.

That said, it can feel time-taxing. You invest a lot of effort into missions only to hit a repetition wall. Once you learn AI spawn locations and routes, it becomes predictable. You can literally watch players farm the same bots in the same areas because they behave consistently.

I’d love to see:

Vehicles to move around the map more dynamically.

Vendors expanded and improved.

Heavier AI tweaks with more randomness and unpredictability.

More dynamic behavior to prevent bot farming.

Continued work on object collision and getting stuck on geometry.

There are still bugs. There are still performance and interaction issues. It’s clearly early access.

But the foundation? Strong.

The gun systems are fantastic. The risk-reward loop is addictive. The world design is beautiful.

It needs work — but it’s new, and I’m genuinely excited to see where it goes.

Recommended.

Alright. Let's talk a little about [i]Gray Zone Warfare[/i], which at the time of this writing, has seen the release of the Spearhead update and witnessed quite a spike in new players, returning players, and overall concurrent and peak player counts. This was my entry point for the game as well. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3702794091

This game is still in what the devs call a "pre-Alpha" build, which is to say that despite being available in early access since April 2024, still has quite a ways to go before it sees its final release and the level of polish you'd expect from a full release (presumably).

At this moment however, this is actually a fully playable and hella fun game, albeit with some significant issues that you would expect from a game in such an early [i]early access[/i] state. Actually, it's one of the few moments where I feel like the value is already there, even with its flaws.

Where the game truly shines is with its gunplay and traversal, in my opinion. Combat feels good. Guns have weight to them. Bullets seem to have real impact. The audio for this is top tier and really adds to the overall feeling that you're really firing actual weapons. Other than the default knife everybody gets. That thing is fairly useless, lol. But yeah. combat is stellar. Traversal also feels good. Walking around/running around is appropriate the setting, which is tropical with some towns and such. There's actually good variety on the map, and the map itself is pretty big, even with the exclusion zone in the center. It's rare that you will experience clipping or get stuck on random objects.

Of course, you can use LZs to infiltrate or exfil via chopper. Which is pretty cool. Especially when the LZ is a significant distance from your faction base. The flights to and fro don't get boring to me. Speaking of factions, you can choose one of three PMCs to be a member of. Your choice does seem to impact things in the game. At the most basic level, this includes which players you can team up with. Since they also need to be part of your PMC. On the map, you can see any fellow mercs who are near you, which is often helpful even when not directly or meaningfully teaming up with them.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3702295060

There are a lot of available quests all along the map in this world and especially after reaching a certain threshold. While the quests do sometimes get a bit repetitive, and despite some of the objectives being...ummm...objectively difficult to track or resolve properly, there is actually a good mix of them. The rewards are solid for each, and some of the harder ones include multiple stages or items required to complete them. They also raise your reputation with vendors in the game, which is very important because it unlocks larger store selections and notably some of the less common ammo that you will need, especially if you invested in the upgrade editions, which feature weapons with pretty rare ammo. Not to mention gun parts, guns themselves, better packs, and so on. This system is already solid. I expect it will keep getting better.

Now to some of the negatives: for one, if you didn't join up with your friends at the same time, or got the game later and thought to play a bit before teaming up with them, you might be out of luck. Why? Because you only get one character, and in order to change PMCs, you will need to delete that character and all its progress in order to start over. This is impactful because you can't really play with friends unless you're all in the same PMC. The co-op aspect of this game is something I think Madfinger needs to address. You should be able to either co-op with friends regardless of your PMC or have a second character slot to use for said co-op. IMO anyway.

If you die in the game, you have a certain window of time to get back to your body and loot it. Otherwise, you are SOL and will probably lose some valuable gear. That in and of itself is not really a big deal. But what does suck is a lot of your activated quests autofail when you die. And all your progress in said quests is lost. Since you can go back to your body and reclaim your gear as long as it's within a certain time parameter AND you don't die on your way there, that should also extend to quest progress. You should only lose quest progress if you also lose the ability to loot your body.

Ultimately, those are procedural gripes. The real issue right now is server stability and rubber banding. The servers crash on the regular. It's kind of funny when everyone is finally able to log back in and people are just chatting around the base about the crash. But it's a truly significant issue at this moment.

What I'm calling rubberbanding is basically where you'll be running and all of a sudden, you're booted back twenty feet. This also happens on the regular.

The final significant issue I've been encountering is the game freezing. Clearly due to the game stressing CPUs. These freezes typically last for ten to twenty seconds. A weird aspect of this is whatever you were doing when it froze, your character continues to do for a second or two while the game was frozen. Which can place you in some real awkward situations, especially if you were in the middle of a gunfight at that moment.

Another thing I don't really enjoy is how insanely accurate some enemies can be, even with fully automatic weapons, and even at extreme distances. And they never seem to hit your armor. Always extremities. Which are insanely accurate shots, especially when your weapon is full auto and not designed to really do that exact thing. There definitely needs to be some more work done with balancing. Yes, the random starter area bandits are pushovers, but further out you go, the more challenging the enemies become, and it feels a bit cheap to have them be the most gigachad of gigachads all day every day regardless of what weapons they have.  Stealth is also objectively useless once you get within like 150 meters of enemies regardless of cover or other factors. Absent nighttime and rainstorms, which does put enemies at a real disadvantage always.

One final gripe: our mercs have the worst cardio known to man. Their low stamina suggests they have spent zero time rucking and all have severe asthma. Let's get those meters raised up significantly.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3699475080

That's about it. I think the game is actually worth buying right now despite the issues I listed, and while I generally am not a proponent of buying upgrade editions, they do have merit here. Rather than placing everything behind paywalls, they just offer better versions of what you get regardless and give you instant access to some gear you would otherwise need to grind to get. Since they're easily lost, this doesn't feel unfair at all. I've only played PvE, but I'd guess pretty much all the PvP players have the upgrade packs, so maybe give PvE a try first and see if the game is fun enough for you to justify buying an upgrade. For me, it was/is.

After 100 hours, I think Gray Zone Warfare’s biggest problem isn’t simply a lack of content. It’s a lack of depth.

The graphics and atmosphere are genuinely good. When you first start playing, especially in the starting area, there is real tension. You’re thinking about where enemies might come from, where you should move, whether you should take cover, and how carefully you need to approach an area.

That was exactly what I wanted from this game. But as you progress, that feeling almost completely disappears.

The map is huge, but it also feels very dead. After visiting the same location a few times, you start memorizing exactly where the same groups of NPCs spawn. Same positions, same enemies, same encounters. Eventually the gameplay becomes: land at an LZ, sprint toward the objective, shoot whoever is in the way, complete the task, and leave.

At that point it stops feeling like a tactical shooter and starts feeling much more like an arcade shooter.

The AI doesn’t help either. Difficulty and bullet sponges are not the same thing. An NPC surviving two or three shots to the head doesn’t make the combat more difficult in an interesting way. It just makes it frustrating.

At the same time, the game itself is not very punishing. In 100+ hours I have only died a few times.

I expected the game to force me to think tactically.

If I’m going into a building, I want to prepare for CQB. If I’m operating in open terrain, I want a different weapon and optic setup. I want my loadout to matter depending on the mission.

But right now, it really doesn’t.

You can run an SVD inside buildings and do CQB perfectly fine. You can buy an M4A1 near the beginning of the game and, as long as you don’t die, use basically the same rifle for the entire progression.

Weapon variety is already quite limited, so you end up using the same guns over and over again. The only meaningful upgrades are usually one or two optics and maybe a suppressor. Even suppressors don’t have enough gameplay impact to make them feel important.

Because of that, preparing a loadout never really becomes an actual decision.

The controls for tactical equipment are also unnecessarily tiring. Flashlights, lasers and similar attachments are all handled through the same control system, and while it’s tolerable at first, after many hours it becomes annoying.

Mission design is probably the game’s biggest problem.

From a story perspective, you might technically be doing different things, but from a gameplay perspective most missions are basically the same:

Run somewhere.

Kill 3 or 4 NPCs.

Walk up to an object.

Press F.

Run another 400 meters.

Press F on another object.

Repeat.

There are roughly 220 missions, but the core gameplay loop barely changes.

The loot system also feels pointless.

Most of the time, the only reason I search the environment is to find food and water. NPCs rarely carry anything worth taking apart from keys. Their weapons even seem to have the same durability values over and over again: around 49%, 52%, or sometimes 100% if you’re lucky.

So most of the time, I don’t even have a reason to search the body of an enemy I just killed.

The map is also full of junk loot. Lighters, fishing line and similar items are everywhere, but most of them currently serve little to no meaningful purpose.

And I don’t want the game to “fix” its lack of depth by adding systems like “collect 30 lighters to upgrade something.”

That’s not the kind of depth I’m talking about.

I want tactical depth.

Before going on a mission, I want to actually think:

Where am I going?

Is it CQB?

Is it open terrain?

Is it night?

Which weapon makes the most sense?

Which optic should I use?

Do I need a flashlight?

Do I need a laser?

Does a suppressor matter here?

Should I change my loadout because I’m expecting close-range combat?

Right now, the answer to most of those questions is basically:

“It doesn’t matter.”

Vertical audio is also a serious problem. Enemies above or below you often sound like they are on the exact same floor. On top of that, there is this endless, extremely annoying insect/fly buzzing sound in some areas that becomes unbearable after a while.

There also isn’t much of an endgame.

If you really want to, you can have someone help you reach one of the hardest areas in the game with nothing but a pistol, kill two or three NPCs, loot their weapons, and you’re basically set.

Even areas that are supposed to be among the most dangerous in the game are surprisingly easy to clear with a Glock once you understand how the AI works.

The foundation of Gray Zone Warfare is not bad.

Actually, the atmosphere, concept and overall framework have the potential to become something very good.

But right now the game makes me feel less like I’m preparing for a military operation and more like I’m doing this:

Land at an LZ.

Run.

Kill the same NPCs.

Press F.

Go back.

Adding more weapons would be nice, but that alone won’t fix the problem.

Adding more loot won’t fix it either.

What the game really needs is systems that force the player to plan, use different equipment, scout locations, adapt to different situations and make meaningful tactical decisions.

If the developers can achieve that, Gray Zone Warfare could become a genuinely great game.

Right now, the atmosphere is good and the foundation is solid, but the tactical depth is still very shallow.

This game has a very important place in gaming. You can choose whether or not you want PVE or PVP. While there are factions, you can change factions without too much hassle (within limits). Unlike games like ABI or Tarkov, Gray Zone doesn't have a forced extraction timer (which I love. I hate timers). The game, while it does have issues because it is STILL IN DEVELOPMENT, is worth playing. You can play at your own pace and be fine if you just play smart. There are developer updates coming soon that should improve the game for many people. The second of which SHOULD give some needed QOL.

Please do not listen to the majority of negative reviews.

1) While you do die in the game (its a combat game, duh) you have 1 chance to regain your lost items. I have died dozens of times and never permanently lost my gear in the last 2 weeks or so.

2) Performance issues. The game is in development, and that causes some performance dips. Let the devs do their thing. I have a EVGA 3080TI GPU, and I run around 45 - 60+ frames ( I am locked from higher frames due to my monitor refresh rate of 60HZ). I do get frame dips, but that is to be expected from a game being heavily developed.

3) While the AI do have some aimbot specifics that are insanely agrivating, you can work around it by paying attention to your environment. If you want to see 2 people that know how to play the game perfectly fine, look up on twitch Jarh3ad_TV and Credard. You will see how the game plays without relying on stupid negative reviews.

4) Some people have claimed that the "DLC's" in the game are a scam. They are not. The DLC's support the developers making the game. They can't build the game properly without income. The DLC editions to the game give you higher stash, some cosmetic items, lots of medical supplies, and few other things. Obviously, if you go out and die and do not get your body back, your items are gone. GO OUT AND GET MORE ITEMS. It's not difficult, especially if I can do it solo with my PTSD and rage issues coupled with my eyesight problems. The phrase "geht gud" here applies perfectly.

5) The game is quite playable as is. The above mentioned streamers have played by selling all of their gear and starting with just a knife. Played with only sniper rifles, or not silenced weapons. I have seen Jar3ead_TV play and entire storyline run with NO SCOPE (not even iron sights). Jar3ad_TV and Credard are among the game experts (there are others, I just do not know them right now). Listen to them. Not the neggative reviews.

This game is entirely what you make of it. If you are unsure, watch people play it live, ask questions, etc. Please do not trash this game simply to trash it. This game is not meant to be COD, its not meant to be Battlefield, or Tarkov. It is meant to be its own game, and it works very well.

I have spent a significant amount of time playing Gray Zone Warfare and initially enjoyed the core gameplay concept. The open-world tactical approach has a lot of potential. Unfortunately, my recent experience with the anti-cheat and support process left me with serious concerns about how moderation and account suspensions are handled.

Approximately two weeks ago, my account was suddenly suspended for what support described as “repeated synthetic or assisted inputs detected in gameplay.” I do not use cheats, macros, scripts, or automation software. Because of this, I contacted support and fully cooperated with their investigation.

During the investigation they requested extensive information about my system, including:

my DxDiag system report

details about my hardware specifications

information about my Razer mouse and keyboard

confirmation that I did not have Razer Synapse or macro software installed

screenshots of my Windows mouse and keyboard settings

I provided everything they requested in order to help clarify the situation.

After almost 15 days, the ban was lifted and I was allowed to return to the game. However, support stated that their system still detected “synthetic inputs” but that they cannot disclose what triggered the detection for security reasons.

From a player’s perspective, this process is frustrating and concerning. Being banned for two weeks for something I did not do, followed by a statement that a violation occurred but without any explanation or evidence, does not feel like a fair or transparent system.

My issue is not simply the temporary suspension — it is the lack of transparency and accountability in the anti-cheat process. Players should have some form of meaningful explanation when their accounts are restricted, especially after cooperating fully with an investigation.

Gray Zone Warfare still has potential as a game, but situations like this make it difficult to trust the moderation and anti-cheat systems.

I hope the developers improve the clarity, transparency, and review process for anti-cheat cases so that players are not left in the dark about what actually triggered a suspension.

If the developers ever provide clarification about what caused the detection in my case, I would gladly update this review.

Almost 1 year after GZW launched into early access and unfortunately I cannot recommend the game for a few important reasons.

Reason 1:  Game still experiences frequent crashes and instability even on servers that are well below the player cap.  The game usually crashes about every 30-45 minutes with de-sync causing battles vs the AI to be like fighting a terminator.

Reason 2:  The AI in the starter towns are using tier 1 ammo and severly damaged weapons but they STILL 1 shot the player to the chest even when equipped with tier 3 armor.  The AI also still track the player through walls and fences with pin-point accuracy.

These two issues have been persistent since the games launch into early access and have still not been addressed a year later.

Reason 3:  With the new updates to the game we now have durability for weapons and armor as well as attachments.  This is nothing new in these types of games but the issue is the durability loss on the armor.  The AI in the starting areas use tier 1 (soft point) ammo but 2 shots to a helmet or 3-4 shots to tier 3 armor will completely destroy them.  Once destroyed you can not repair anything, armor or weapons/attachments.  This makes even early game battles very costly and removes the benefit of doing the early game quests.

The game has potential but, as per usual, it seems like the game devs focus is on pushing out more and more content rather than ironing out the problems with the content they already have.  Gamers do not want to invest hours into a game when they could be 1 shot in their best gear by a low level AI using basic tier ammo and armor or crash 30 minutes into a mission.  I have invested almost 90 hours into the game so far and recently returned to check out the state of the game before the 1 year anniversary of launch only to find it in worse condition than it was at the beginning.

Update: Players are still leaving in droves because the problems with the AI persist.  56% player drop-off in 1 month and a continued decline over 3 due to (mostly) AI 1 taps through armor and tracking through cover.  The game has such great potential, please don't just give us a reason to come back, give us a reason to stay.

I'm not usually a Realistic Mill-sim gamer, i do find this game fun. At least for the first 30 hours. Afterwards it went downhill quite fast.
I always take it slow. No running when im in an area with potential enemies. Suppressor at all times if possible. Scout before shooting, all the "safe" ways of playing.
At first if i were spotted, i'd be hit a few times, be in danger zone health, but be able to either revenge my shots or get away and heal with what was necessary - WHEN it made sense.
I had fun, things were a bit slow, but i was enjoying my time. Getting some.. good loot.
But then it started happening..
No time to react, no time to get a feeling where the enemies were. I'd just be dead. One shot. No counterplay.
Check steam clip, not a single enemy in sight.
The AI im shooting survives 5-6 bullets to upper chest/ neck. runs back, hides. Shoots a single time - im dead.
How? Why?
He shot me in the arm and it ricocheted into my lungs. Or.. at least thats what death screen tells me.
I havent been able to once for the last 7 hours, to disengage. Since i'd be dead in one shot.

I get it. It's realistic, maybe im too out in the open, maybe i have too low NIJ Armor value. Maybe my ammo type was too weak. Nope, checked it all. All should've pointed to me surviving at least 2 shots. (When applicable, such as chest shots)

And it kept going. And whenever i wanted to loot, the loot would already have been taken. Then why should i be in the higher areas? 
Spending 15 minutes just to get through Sawmill, to it be empty, simply ruins it for me.
Having loot be shared between all players, with a game which is meant to be slower, doesn't make sense to me.
Should all loot be "private"? No. But if loot should be shared between all, there should be more options. (I understand, this is being worked on for 0.4)

I have trouble recommending it, in its current state. It's not bad, but you should definitely bring at least one friend. 
Being a usual solo player, it's rough. For a Duo team, it's definitely worth your time. 
At the current moment i have basically seen all there is to see. I do expect to play again in 0.4.
And in the terms of gameplay loop. Great, fantastic. Please keep it. I love doing the quests. Though i would hope they become more fleshed out. Right now they're just "inspect a, go to b, see c" And please make objective items more noticeable.
Only nod towards what you're supposed to do is the text from the mission objective. Which is fine, but having walked past a notebook multiple times, because the UI is a bit slow and the notebook COMPLETELY blends with the enviroment is a bit iffy.

TL;DR: If you're okay with a very early access game that still has a lot of issues then I say get it! It's a load of fun when issues aren't happening. When they do happen though, it will frustrate you to no end.

If you do decide to get it, I would highly recommend getting the base edition first to see if it's the right fit for you. The edition upgrades are classed as DLC so they are not eligible for a refund if you decide you do not like it.

I still cannot recommend it to the average gamer yet however so as of now, it will stay as not recommended.

--- EDIT: 5/2/24 ---

After two days, I finally was able to obtain my supporter edition items after a character reset. 

I anticipated this would be the fix, so I haven't really played since the first night, but I will update my original review after the hotfixes to see how things have been improving.

--- EDIT: 5/8/24 ---

After Hotfix 3, a major issue where servers would depopulate after 30-45 minutes has been resolved. 

This game has been making major improvements within the first weeks of it's release.

My review will still remain as Not Recommended until they get a handle on server performance, crashes, and optimization.

-- EDIT: 9/10/26 --
Still sits as a not recommended title for me. The development time has been abysmally slow, two years later and we're finally entering Alpha?? Is this the next Star Citizen? I've been keeping an eye on this game, but nothing has changed significantly enough in the past two years for me to pick it up again.

--End of Edit--

THE BAD:

During the first few days, I encountered issues with getting my supporter edition items and loot from missions, however this was fixed with a character reset introduced in Hotfix 2.

PERFORMANCE: Performance and Optimization is not good. I have an i7-12700kf and a 3070ti with 32GB of RAM, and I struggle to get 60 FPS on high settings. (On the latest drivers).

SERVER PERFORMANCE: Audio constantly cuts in and out, and rubber banding is a constant issue, which gets worse the longer you're in the server. Server performance definitely needs improvements. AI dying is delayed, sometimes they drop a couple seconds after being shot

TEAM DYNAMIC: Teamkilling is slowly getting better, but is still a more common than it should be issue. I still stand by the idea that teamkilling needs to either have punishments or maybe if you get teamkilled, your loot cannot be taken by friendly forces. Removing it completely however does not make sense for this kind of game. 

Some servers, you get Seal Team Six qualified teammates, other times you get teammates that blast you after you announce yourself 5 times and then act shocked. It really depends.

GAMEPLAY: The Movement, gunplay, and AI needs a lot of work. AI is pretty tanky and inhuman. They just stand there, and then when they aggro, unless you get a nice clean headshot, sometimes you clear an entire mag before they drop. On this note, AI can see you through bushes and start blasting even when you haven't laid your eyes on them yet.

They definitely need to add a reaction to AI when they are shot, I completely understand that a shot to the vest won't kill them, however, they should at least fall/kneel over in pain. 

To add to this point, it's also frankly very frustrating when AI insta one-taps you to the head. It's clear that there isn't a suppression effect for AI. 

Movement is very choppy, buggy animations, and teleport vaulting (I just appear on the other side of the wall with no animation periodically). 

LOOTING: This is a hard topic to really give an answer on, with looting, I feel like I don't come back with much new gear even after a successful run. The looting needs work, but this is out of my scope to give an answer on what should change.

GENERAL BUGS: The headless glitch seems to have been fixed in Hotfix 3, I haven't seen anymore headless characters yet.

Another issue I noticed is that completing the first mission for the medic lady (forgot her name off the top of my head) I handed over the required item, and it took it from my inventory but still asked me to hand it over and the mission remained incomplete. I'm going to run the mission again and see if it works the second time around.

BEWARE: edition upgrades are classed as DLC so you can't get the money back if you decide to refund.

The OK/GOOD:

GUNPLAY: Gunplay isn't TERRIBLE but it's not great either. For the type of game this is, I was expecting guns to feel a little more powerful. Gunplay is in an "arcady" state right now IMO. 

The M4 power wise is great, the AK on the other hand, I'm not really sure if it's bugged, but it just feels so much weaker than the M4. I've noticed it takes a lot more hits to kill with an AK vs M4 even using FMJ.

Reloading the base SKS, your character must have arthritis in his hands or something because dear lord is the reload painfully slow.

Pistols also need a lot of work power wise, they look and sound great, but it shoots like it's a toy replica.

GRAPHICS: Frankly, The graphics are good. They are satisfying and immersive visuals. The only gripe I have for graphics is targets downrange can be VERY hard to see. Grayzone is frankly a beautiful game.



HEALTH SYSTEM: The health system is really cool as well. It's immersive enough that you have to take a second to decide the best treatment of your conditions, but not too immersive to the point of needing a PHD to understand it 

EXTRACTION: The Base and LZ systems are also good. I like that you get the emotional satisfaction of physically extracting the AO.

The UI/Inventory system, is passable for an Alpha build. No praises but no gripes either as of now. It's just very barebones atm.

Conclusion:

Grayzone is a promising game that released a little earlier than it probably should have for it's own good. With time, I feel like it will be a great game. 

At this time however, I cannot recommend it for the general gamer. For gamers that are okay with very early access, I say go for it. If you're the type of gamer that likes a little bit of polish, this game isn't there quite yet.

I really wish I didn’t have to say this. Because I like this game. The map, the concept ... BUT ...

TASKS AND PROGRESSION:
Same mundane, boring task system as almost every other failed extraction shooter. “Take this box of food and medicine and drop it by a house next to the road” — meanwhile you’re getting shot at by AI from that same house. Everything wrong with Tarkov’s task system, multiplied by 100. There’s zero creativity, even in naming the tasks. Task name: “Negotiator.” Task description: “Find the negotiator.” Honestly, it feels like the tasks are AI-generated. Coming from Tarkov and looking for something new and refreshing, the progression and task design pushed me straight back to Customs, hunting for that pocket bronze watch.

MOVEMENT:
Movement is awful. You get stuck on the smallest objects. Vaulting barely works. A short sprint and two jumps, and your character sounds like he’s about to have a stroke.

AI:
The AI is awful — in every possible way. I’ve had enemies walk right past me without noticing, and the next second I’m being shot through walls. The moment I hear “RELOADING,” I peek — and instantly get lasered in the face. And why are the native Lamang fighters giving each other callouts in English??? “He’s running!” “He’s going left!” Honestly, what the fuck.

IMMERSION:
NONE. And I mean NONE. The only time I actually feel immersed is when I’m walking around trying to find new LZs — that’s it. PVP is barely engaging. It mostly happens in LZs or outposts. LZs are just camping, and outposts are glorified camping. The NPC voice lines? Maybe four sets of conversations, fifteen lines max. Every time I start to feel like I’m part of the world, I hear the same recycled dialogue, get shot from the same house I’m delivering food to, or hear indigenous fighters yelling callouts to each other in ... ENGLISH.

This game has so much potential. Honestly, out of all the extraction shooters I’ve played — besides Tarkov — this one could’ve been something special. But here I am, pissed and unimpressed.

There are bugs and that is expected, I do believe the game's launch has been rushed and should've rather been in Summer allowing the developers time to fix the performance issues and learn more about the game's bugs through a closed early access release with people of different PC specs ranging from low-end to high-end and not just have one play-test for creators whom usually have very high-spec PCs. The game has the best gun sound system I've seen in any game and the gun physics are impeccable as well. Having no load screens after deploying to the end of your deployment adds that realism aspect that few games have reached in the past. The game-play cycle is fun and exciting giving the player a variety of choices whether they want to play PvEvP, PvE and exactly what to do in those modes (hunt players/ai, complete vendor tasks, hang out with friends in a squad). The health system is fun in a way where it's not too overwhelming but you will have to plan out every move to ensure that you are not being shot and have to heal making yourself vulnerable for a moderate period of time.

Overall I believe the game's release was rushed hence causing performance drops but the actual game itself is a very fun open-world FPS game with it's unique twists and overwhelmingly good graphics. The gun system is one of the best I've seen in terms of the physics and sounds as well. I recommend the game to anyone with a high-spec PC for now while the performance optimization still lacks and hope in the future this issue is addressed and improved greatly to ensure the whole spectrum of PCs can play the game.

Gray Zone Warfare – Not Recommended (For Now)

Gray Zone Warfare has potential. The core gameplay loop is there, but the current execution is rough, to say the least.

The updates so far have been small and haven’t done much to push the game forward. Visibility is a mess. At times, it feels like it was made for people who play with their eyes closed. Whether it’s the lighting, clutter, foliage, or upscaling, it often works against you instead of helping you play the game.

Performance is also in a bad spot. It runs about as well as Star Citizen. Frame drops and generally low FPS are common, even on decent hardware.

The sound design doesn’t help either. Sometimes you hear shots and can't tell if it’s aimed at you or your buddy five buildings away. It’s inconsistent and confusing, which makes situational awareness a real challenge.

Gunplay is... hard to explain. It just doesn’t feel right. Shooting feels clunky, and there’s very little feedback when firing or handling weapons. It’s like the guns are just floating in your hands, disconnected from any real sense of weight or impact.

AI has improved a bit. At least bots don’t beam you through bushes anymore, so that’s something. But they’re still a mess. Sometimes they miss everything, and sometimes they one-tap you from a bush like they’ve been camping there all day. It’s not fun, and you often don’t even get the chance to react or heal before getting dropped. Other times they just stand in the open like cardboard cutouts with rifles, barely responding even when you’re lighting them up.

In short, Gray Zone Warfare could eventually be something special, but it’s not there yet. The foundation is solid, but performance, AI, gunplay, sound design, and overall polish need serious attention. For now, it’s one to keep an eye on, not one to play.
